figs.title: Contour families
figs.caption: The Hessian eigenvalues set the contour shape: both positive give ellipses, mixed signs give hyperbolas, and a zero eigenvalue gives parallel lines with a valley of minima. The eigenvectors of H give the principal axes through the critical point x* = −H⁻¹b.

figs.title: Strong Wolfe step lengths
figs.caption: The Armijo line has slope c₁φ′(0) and accepts steps where φ lies below it. Strong Wolfe also requires |φ′(α)| ≤ c₂|φ′(0)|, which keeps the accepted steps near local minimizers of φ.

figs.title: Trust region dogleg
figs.caption: The dogleg path runs from xₖ to the Cauchy point along −g, then toward the Newton point, and the step is where the path meets the trust-region boundary ‖p‖ = Δ. When the Newton point lies inside the region, the full Newton step is taken.

figs.title: KKT geometry at a corner
figs.caption: At a corner optimum, −∇f lies in the cone spanned by the outward gradients of the active constraints, so −∇f = μ₁∇g₁ + μ₂∇g₂ with μᵢ ≥ 0. Each multiplier measures the sensitivity of the optimal f to relaxing its constraint.

figs.title: Penalty versus barrier
figs.caption: An exterior quadratic penalty places the minimizer slightly outside the feasible set and approaches the boundary as ρ grows. A log barrier keeps iterates strictly feasible and approaches the boundary as μ shrinks.

figs.title: Pareto front and weighted sums
figs.caption: Every Pareto point is nondominated, and the utopia point combines the individual minima of each objective. A weighted sum reaches only points on the convex hull of the front, so the ε-constraint method is used for nonconvex regions.

figs.title: Constraint diagram
figs.caption: Each constraint gives a minimum T_SL/W_TO as a function of W_TO/S, and the landing field length sets a maximum W_TO/S. The design point is the lowest thrust loading in the feasible region, taken at the highest wing loading that reaches it.

figs.title: Power required and available
figs.caption: Parasite power grows as V³ and induced power falls as 1/V, so total power required has a minimum at V_mp, where induced power is three times parasite power. The line from the origin tangent to P_R marks minimum drag and maximum L/D, the best range speed for a propeller aircraft.

figs.title: V-n diagram
figs.caption: The stall curves are parabolas n = (V/V_S)² that meet the limit load at the corner speed V_A = V_S√n_max. Gust lines radiate from n = 1 at zero speed with slope proportional to the gust velocity, and V_D closes the envelope.

figs.title: Turbofan ideal T-s diagram
figs.caption: The core follows isentropic compression from 0 to 3, isobaric heat addition from 3 to 4, and isentropic expansion through the turbine and nozzle to 9 at p₀. The bypass stream is compressed from 2 to 13 and expands isentropically to p₀, so in the ideal cycle station 19 returns to the ambient static temperature with higher velocity.

figs.title: Turbofan station numbering
figs.caption: Core stations run 0 freestream, 2 fan face, 3 compressor exit, 4 turbine inlet, 5 turbine exit and 9 core nozzle exit. The bypass stream uses 13 at the fan exit and 19 at the bypass nozzle exit.

figs.title: Horseshoe vortex and elliptic lift
figs.caption: A horseshoe vortex has a bound segment of strength Γ along the quarter chord and two trailing vortices that induce downwash between them. An elliptic circulation distribution gives uniform downwash and the minimum induced drag, C_Di = C_L²/(πAR).

figs.title: Actuator disk in hover
figs.caption: The stream tube contracts as the flow accelerates from rest far upstream to v_i at the disk and 2v_i in the far wake, where the area is half the disk area. Thrust equals the momentum flux in the wake, T = 2ρAv_i².

figs.title: Climbing turn free body
figs.caption: Thrust acts at α + ε to the velocity vector, lift is perpendicular to it in the plane of symmetry, drag opposes it and weight acts vertically. Resolving along and normal to the flight path at climb angle γ gives the point-mass equations of motion.

figs.title: Pressure vessel stresses
figs.caption: A half-cylinder free body balances internal pressure p·2r against two hoop forces σ_θt, giving σ_θ = pr/t. In a thick wall the Lamé solution σ = A ± B/r² gives the largest hoop stress at the inner surface and σ_rr equal to −p there and zero at the outer surface.

figs.title: Prandtl membrane analogy
figs.caption: The stress function φ behaves like a pressurized membrane over the cross-section: shear stress equals the membrane slope and torque equals twice the enclosed volume. In a rectangle the steepest slope, and so the maximum shear stress, occurs at the midpoints of the long sides.

figs.title: Buckling archetypes
figs.caption: A stable symmetric bifurcation has a rising postbuckling path and imperfect paths that approach it smoothly. Unstable symmetric and asymmetric bifurcations give imperfect structures a maximum load below P_cr, and a limit point marks snap-through where dP/dw = 0.

figs.title: Rigid bar spring models
figs.caption: A rigid bar of length L on a base spring C under vertical dead load buckles at P_cr = C/L, and its total potential Π = ½Cθ² − PL(1 − cos θ) governs postbuckling. The two-bar chain has two degrees of freedom θ₁ and θ₂, so its stability matrix gives two critical loads.

figs.title: Euler column effective lengths
figs.caption: The Euler load P_cr = π²EI/(KL)² uses the effective length KL, the distance between inflection points of the buckled shape. Pinned-pinned gives K = 1, fixed-free K = 2, fixed-fixed K = 0.5 and fixed-pinned K ≈ 0.7.

figs.title: Coil spring free body
figs.caption: A cut through the wire of a close-coiled spring shows a torque T = PR and a direct shear force P at the wire section. Torsion of the wire dominates the deflection, giving the stiffness k = Gd⁴/(64R³n).

figs.title: Propped cantilever by superposition
figs.caption: Removing the roller leaves a cantilever under w and a cantilever under the tip force R, and zero total deflection at the prop gives R = 3wL/8. The wall then carries a shear of 5wL/8 and a moment of wL²/8.
